claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
The as-fabricated alloy has a relatively homogeneous microstructure with minimal initial oxide presence.
The as-fabricated alloy has high mechanical integrity.
Elevated-temperature degradation is governed by the competitive formation and stability of primarily Al-rich and Cr-rich oxide scales at grain boundaries and interfaces.
Oxidizing atmospheres produce discontinuous or poorly adherent oxide scales at critical intergranular sites.
Discontinuous or poorly adherent intergranular oxides cause local stress concentration and intergranular embrittlement.
Reducing atmospheres prevent or destabilize protective oxide scales.
The absence or instability of protective oxides accelerates atomic diffusion along grain boundaries.
Accelerated grain-boundary diffusion weakens intergranular cohesion and promotes crack initiation.
At high temperatures, selective oxidation occurs at grain boundaries.
Al-rich and Cr-rich oxides formed in oxidizing environments may fail to develop into a continuous protective film.
Thermal-expansion mismatch or oxide-scale spallation creates local stresses at grain boundaries that initiate cracks.
Both oxidation-associated intergranular damage and reducing-atmosphere diffusion-mediated weakening can accelerate crack nucleation and propagation to catastrophic failure.
Relative to as-manufactured specimens, oxidizing exposure will produce intergranular oxides accompanied by localized cracking.
Oxidizing exposure will reduce tensile strength or fracture toughness relative to the starting-state baseline.
Reducing exposure will produce minimal oxide coverage.
Reducing exposure will cause diffusion-related grain-boundary weakening and may produce catastrophic failure comparable to that under oxidizing exposure.
The severity and character of degradation will differ between oxidizing and reducing atmospheres according to the interfacial oxide state.
The proposed mechanism applies approximately from 800 to 1000 degrees Celsius in well-defined oxidizing or reducing gases.
Outside the specified temperature or gas-composition range, different degradation mechanisms may operate.
